caption_used: The performance of knowledge probing after editing with different editing methods on BioMedLM, where "Base" denotes LLM without editing. The x-axis shows co-occurrence number on a logarithmic scale, while the y-axis represents accuracy (ACC %). All six methods show improving accuracy with increasing co-occurrence frequency. ROME consistently achieves the highest accuracy, starting at approximately 51% and reaching roughly 66% at the highest co-occurrence numbers. MEND and MEMIT follow as the next best performers, with MEND reaching approximately 56% and MEMIT approximately 55%. Notably, IKE demonstrates a steeper improvement rate than FT, surpassing it at co-occurrence numbers above 10^2 to reach approximately 52% at the highest frequency. The Base model exhibits the lowest performance throughout, plateauing at approximately 44%.
raw_response:
The plot illustrates the relationship between co-occurrence numbers and accuracy percentages for various editing methods on BioMedLM. The x-axis, labeled "Co-occurrence Number," uses a logarithmic scale, ranging from $10^0$ to $10^3$. The y-axis, labeled "ACC(%)", is linear, spanning from 40% to 65%. 

The plot features six lines, each representing a different method: Base (black, solid, circles), MEND (brown, solid), FT (blue, solid, triangles), MEMIT (purple, solid), IKE (red, solid, triangles), and ROME (green, solid). 

The Base line starts at approximately 39% and reaches around 44% at the highest co-occurrence numbers. The FT line begins at about 40% and reaches approximately 48% at the highest co-occurrence numbers. The IKE line starts at around 42%, surpasses FT at co-occurrence numbers above $10^2$, and reaches approximately 52% at the highest frequency. The MEMIT line begins at around 43% and reaches approximately 55%. The MEND line starts at approximately 43% and reaches around 56%. The ROME line starts at approximately 51% and reaches roughly 66%.
